# Pairwise take-home exercise: candidate guide

This guide is for candidates. It says how the exercise is run, what your repository must contain, what limits apply, and how to check your work before you submit. `EXERCISE.md` says what to build. `openapi.yaml` is the contract for the API.

## 1. Your invitation and your window
<!-- C13.M3 C2.M2 C1.M11 C13.M7 -->

A person at Pairwise sends you an invitation page addressed to you. It gives you:

- a link to this guide, behind the words "How to take a Pairwise exam";
- the command that clones the exercise files;
- a Start button, which opens your exam page, where you start and submit;
- the date to press Start by;
- your window and grace period;
- your run limit and your stage limits, in minutes and seconds;
- whom to contact with questions;
- that the source you submit and its results are kept indefinitely.

Your window starts only when you press Start on your exam page, and you must press it within the start window. If the start window lapses, or you lose the invitation, contact the person who sent you the invitation. They can send you a new invitation. The invitation link works for 7 days; ask for a fresh one after that. The receipt time of a submission is the moment your exam page is used. It is not the date of a commit.

## 2. What must be in your repository
<!-- C3.M2 C3.M3 C3.M4 -->

Your repository must contain these four files at these paths:

- `services/api/Dockerfile`
- `services/worker/Dockerfile`
- `services/web/Dockerfile`
- `harness.yaml`

A run that lacks any of them fails at the `validate` stage. Each service is built from its own directory, `services/<name>`, so anything a service needs, including its tests, lives inside that directory. Do not commit a `.git` folder inside your repository.

`harness.yaml` has three keys. The kit's file is the example:

```yaml
version: 1
tests:
  service: api
  command: ["python", "-c", "print('no tests yet')"]
```

`version` is `1`. `tests.service` is one of `api`, `worker` or `web`, the service whose running container runs your tests. `tests.command` is a list of strings, not one string. `./pw-check` does a short check of this file; a run checks it in full.

`DESIGN.md` and `AI-USAGE.md` are required for assessment. A run records whether they are present and does not fail without them.

## 3. The services and the network
<!-- C3.M5 C3.M6 C9.M5 C9.M6 -->

- `api` listens on port 8000 and serves the API in `openapi.yaml` as JSON.
- `web` listens on port 3000 and answers `GET /` with HTML.
- `worker` listens on no port.

Every service gets these environment variables from the pack: `DATABASE_URL` and `API_URL`. `api` and `web` also get `PORT`, which is 8000 for `api` and 3000 for `web`. Reach Postgres only through `DATABASE_URL`, which points at `postgres.pw.internal:5432`. Reach `api` at `api.pw.internal:8000` and `web` at `web.pw.internal:3000`.

Do not use `postgres`, `toxiproxy` or any other Compose service name, and do not use the reserved `pw.internal` names other than the three above. Look names up with the system resolver, such as Node's `dns.lookup`, not `dns.resolve`.

## 4. What a run does
<!-- C3.M7 -->

A run goes through eight stages, in order: fetch, unpack, validate, build, up, smoke, tests and collect.

- **Before Compose runs**, the run deletes any compose file, any `.env` file and any `.pw-out` directory at the root of your repository. A compose file inside a service directory is your own file; the run does not touch it.
- **build** builds your three services. Runs build for `linux/amd64` and services run under gVisor (`runsc`); `pw-check` builds for your own machine.
- **up** starts Postgres and your three services.
- **smoke** runs the smoke test described in `EXERCISE.md`.
- **tests** runs your test command in the running container of `tests.service`. It is run as an argument list, with no shell and no terminal. It runs even if the smoke test failed. Its output is cut to its last 50 MB.
- **collect** gathers the logs and results.

## 5. Checking locally with `./pw-check`
<!-- C3.M7 C9.M3 -->

`./pw-check` needs Docker with Compose and nothing else. It builds your services, starts the stack, waits for the services, and runs the same smoke test as a run, then prints one line for each of the five checks and tears the stack down. It exits 0 if the smoke test passes, 1 if a check fails, and 2 if it could not run.

It differs from a run:

- it uses Docker's default runtime, not gVisor;
- it applies no resource limits;
- it does not run your tests;
- it records nothing.

Under `./pw-check`, outside names and Compose service names resolve. In a run they do not. Do not depend on them.

On Apple silicon, `./pw-check` builds `arm64` images. `DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM=linux/amd64 ./pw-check` checks the `amd64` build under emulation, slowly.

The kit's `compose.yaml` sits at the root of your repository. A run deletes it, so editing it changes `./pw-check` only. A run uses Pairwise's copy. `./pw-check` warns if your copy differs from the kit's.

## 6. Hosting your work
<!-- C3.M1 C2.M5 C2.M13 -->

Your exam page tells you which of two ways applies to you.

**A private repository, made for you.** Your exam page shows its address. When you press Start, the page asks for your GitHub user name, and GitHub will email you an invitation to your submission repository: accept it, clone the repository and push your work there. It starts as a copy of this kit. You can push branches and new tags, but you cannot move or delete a tag once it is pushed. Your access ends when a submission's build has passed, when your due time and grace period pass, or when your exam is closed. Pairwise keeps the repository for 90 days after your exam closes, then deletes it.

**A public repository.** Put your work in a public repository, on any git host that can be cloned over `https` without credentials. The repository URL starts with `https://`. Submodules and large-file objects are not fetched. To start, use `c2-template` as a GitHub template ("Use this template"), or download the zip from the kit link and push it to a new public repository.

## 7. Submitting
<!-- C2.M1 C2.M3 C2.M4 C2.M5 C2.M6 C2.M7 C2.M8 C2.M10 C2.M11 C2.M13 C1.M7 C4.M11 C5.M2 -->

Press Start on your exam page, then give the page the git URL of your repository and a tag or a full 40-character commit hash. With a private repository the form asks for the tag only, because the page already knows your repository. A branch is not accepted. Pushing a tag is recommended. A tag name starts with a letter, a digit or an underscore, and contains no `..`. A commit hash works only where the host serves a commit by its ID, so a tag is safer. The tag is fixed to its commit when you submit, so later pushes are not assessed.

The URL has at most 2,000 characters and carries no password. The scheme is `https`.

A bad field shows the form again with a message and creates no run. That holds even when no form is offered, because a bad field is refused before the offer is checked.

Your exam page shows one of seven states, the first of these that applies, and every page after Start shows your due time and the end of your grace period:
<!-- states in the order of fixtures/c2/page-states.json -->

- **Lapsed**: you did not press Start in time: contact the person who sent your invitation, who can send you a new invitation <!-- state: Lapsed -->
- **Not started**: your window, grace period, run limit and stage limits, the date to press Start by, and Start <!-- state: Not started -->
- **Received**: the receipt time, and that your repository is being fetched <!-- state: Received -->
- **Accepted**: the receipt time and the commit, and the form again while it is offered <!-- state: Accepted -->
- **Window over**: that the submission window is over, and the reason if your latest submission was rejected <!-- state: Window over -->
- **Rejected**: the reason, and the form again <!-- state: Rejected -->
- **Started**: you pressed Start and have not submitted yet: the form <!-- state: Started -->

A submission after your due time but within the grace period is taken and marked late. If a submission is rejected, the page gives the reason, and you can submit again while the form is offered. The reasons are `unreachable`, `ref_not_found`, `too_large`, `timeout`, `unsafe_path` and `repo_not_allowed`:

- `unreachable`: the repository could not be reached without credentials
- `ref_not_found`: the name is not a tag in the repository (a branch is not a tag), or the host would not serve that commit
- `too_large`: the repository is over the fetch size limit
- `timeout`: the fetch did not finish in the fetch time
- `unsafe_path`: the repository holds a file path that cannot be accepted, such as a nested `.git` folder or a path with a backslash
- `repo_not_allowed`: the repository is not your submission repository, which is the only one the portal reads

On a private repository a submission counts once a build has passed, and your access ends then. If the build fails, your exam page offers the form again, up to 5 attempts in all and never while a run is in flight, and the access you have stays. One accepted submission is final. After your invitation is closed, or 180 days after it was sent, the link no longer works.

## 8. AI tools
<!-- C3.M3 -->

AI tools are allowed. `DESIGN.md` and `AI-USAGE.md` are required for assessment, and a run does not fail without them.

## 9. Your data
<!-- C4.M9 C4.M18 -->

The harness holds no personal data. Results carry only a candidate ID. The one exception is the GitHub user name you give for a private repository: it is used to send your invitation and to remove your access, and it is deleted when your access ends or your exam is closed.

## 10. Limits
<!-- C3.M10 C3.M11 -->

Every limit a run applies is in this table. A MB is 1,000,000 bytes and a GB is 1,000,000,000 bytes.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Platform | `linux/amd64`; candidate services run under gVisor (`runsc`). Runs build for `linux/amd64`; `pw-check` builds for your own machine |
| Resources per candidate service | 1 vCPU, 2 GiB of memory, and 512 processes and threads, with a host task backstop of 1,280 |
| Run limit | 60 min unless your invitation says otherwise, never less than 30 min and never more than 120 min |
| Stage time limits | Fractions of the run limit, rounded down to whole seconds: `build` 1/3, `up` 1/9, `smoke` 1/9, `tests` 2/9. At the default run limit these are `build` 20 min, `up` 6 min 40 s, `smoke` 6 min 40 s, `tests` 13 min 20 s. Your invitation gives your own values in minutes and seconds |
| Stop grace | 10 s between `SIGTERM` and `SIGKILL` |
| Fetch | 2 min and 200 MB; one commit, no submodules, no large-file objects |
| Unpacked snapshot | 1 GB and 50,000 entries |
| Network while running | In a harness run, the build can reach the internet and nothing after it can: once the build ends, your services and your test command have no network. Only the `pw.internal` names resolve, from `/etc/hosts` through the system resolver. Any other lookup fails, and a single lookup call waits at most 6 s |
| Window | Press Start within 7 days of your invitation. Your due time is 72 hours after Start by default, then a 24-hour grace period |
| Logs and files | Each log is cut to its last 50 MB; a file over 50 MB is not recorded |
| Retention | Source and results are kept indefinitely; run files and notices are kept for 730 days; invitation pages for at most 180 days; a private submission repository for 90 days after your portal closes |
